section.sectionSummaryBrief: Although the point of fear of Heaven above intellect is beyond limitation, it still has many levels, with its ultimate essence to be revealed in the future.
section.t: Now, even though the point of fear of Heaven that is above intellect is beyond limitation,
nevertheless,
it has within it
(in its revelation)
many levels,
and its true essence will be in the future to come.
And this is that in the future
(specifically)
"Jerusalem will be inhabited as open villages,"
and Rashi explains41
that it will have no measure or limit, etc.
And even then there will be ascents without end,
as Rashi says41
that it will grow from day to day.
And this is "the righteousness of your open villages in Israel... the Holy One, blessed be He, performed charity with Israel by scattering them among the nations,"
for this that is stated in the verse regarding this matter
("charity... that He scattered them...")
is in the language of "open villages,"

because the charity that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed with Israel by scattering them among the nations is that through this they will reach the "open villages" that are above measurement and limitation.
And there are two matters in this.
That through the hindrances and obstacles of the time of exile
(He scattered them among the nations)
the point of fear of Heaven that is in each Jew is aroused and revealed
(as explained at length in the maamar42)
which is above measurement and limitation.
And moreover,
the matter of "open villages" alludes
(as brought above in section 3 of the maamar)
to "Jerusalem will be inhabited as open villages,"
that through the arousal of the point of fear of Heaven in the time of exile,
there will afterwards be an addition and ascent in the point of fear of Heaven,
its essence as it will be in the future.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: In "Jerusalem will be inhabited as open villages" there are two aspects: the point itself is beyond limitation, and its expansion is also unlimited.
section.t: And it can be said,
that in "Jerusalem will be inhabited as open villages"
(the point of fear of Heaven)
there are two matters.
That the point of fear of Heaven itself is beyond limitation
(as above in section 5),
and also its expansion43
is without limit.
And within this itself there are two matters.
That the point of fear of Heaven acts upon all the powers of the soul to be in accordance with the point,
and that also the point itself spreads into all the powers of the soul44,
even into the garments of thought, speech, and action.
And analogous to "Jerusalem will be inhabited as open villages" in its simple sense,
that in addition to Jerusalem being the point of the center of the world and from the foundation stone in the Holy Temple the entire world was founded45,
also Jerusalem itself will spread throughout the entire world,
for in the future Jerusalem will spread throughout all the Land of Israel and the Land of Israel will spread throughout all the lands46.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The term "open villages" also relates to the charity of scattering, as the Torah and mitzvot of one Jew in a place of ease empowers another in a place of decree through the unifying point of fear of Heaven.
section.t: And seemingly one should add,
that this which is stated "open villages"
(and not "scattered"),
the matter of "Jerusalem will be inhabited as open villages,"
also relates to the charity of scattering explained at the beginning of the maamar,
that the involvement in Torah and mitzvot of Jews who are in places of ease gives strength and might to Jews who are in a place of decree so that they can study Torah and fulfill mitzvot.
For this that the involvement in Torah and mitzvot of one gives strength and might to another is because all Jews are one reality,
especially from the aspect of the point of fear of Heaven and their self-nullification,
which is the point that unifies all of Israel.
Therefore,
in order that the involvement in Torah and mitzvot of one gives strength and might to another
(the matter of charity in this that He scattered them)
it is when his involvement in Torah and mitzvot is in the point of fear of Heaven,
"Jerusalem will be inhabited as open villages,"
that his fear of Heaven
(Jerusalem)
is in a manner of "and you shall break forth47
westward and eastward and northward and southward,"
that it spreads and penetrates all the powers of the soul,
even into his thought, speech, and action.
